# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 99 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Athous, Shepherd of Hermas 99 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_099_page_001.jpg

---

## Similitude 9, Chapter 16

**1** "But who are those stones that were cropped all around and thrown far away from the tower?" I asked. **2** "These," he said, "are those who believed but departed from the way of truth. They are the worst of all the sinners, and yet they had a small remnant of faith in them, and because of this something was left in them, and they were thrown far away. **3** But repentance for them is easy; for they only turned away from the truth but committed no transgression against the commandment of God; since the day when they departed, however, they lost what little faith they had." **4** "But who are those with the spots?" **5** "These," he said, "are those who came to faith and lived mostly in righteousness, but had some worldliness attached to them; and therefore they are spotted and not whole." **6** "But who are those who were half-burned?" **7** "Those are the ones who were in contact with the heathen and doubted whether they should remain with the servants of God or with the heathen. They were burned, that is, they sinned somewhat; but since they did not depart from God, they were not utterly burned." **8** "But the cracked ones — who are they?" **9** "Those who had evil thoughts against one another in their hearts and did not make peace among themselves; they had peace in outward appearance only, but when they separated from one another their wicked thoughts remained in their hearts. **10** These are the cracks that were in the stones. But those who repented were healed, for the rest of them who were cracked — repentance restored them." **11** "But those who returned the short stones — who are they?" "These were faithful, but they also had large amounts of double-mindedness, and so they fell short of the full measure. They were short because they always had something of the world attached to them."

---

*EMET: the "half-burned" stones are a distinctive category — partial compromise with pagan society. The "cracked" = inward hostility masked by outward peace.*
